title: Primitive Recursiveness of the Co-Length Prefix
statement: The function that takes a finite Boolean string $xs$ and a natural number $n$ and returns the prefix of $xs$ of length $\max(\operatorname{length}(xs)-n,0)$ is primitive recursive.
replaced:
The two-argument function taking a Boolean string $xs$ and a natural number $n$ to
the prefix of $xs$ of length $\abs{xs} - n$ (truncated subtraction, so the empty
string when $n \ge \abs{xs}$) is primitive recursive.
